raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'll reason in my own voice first, then lay it out properly.

---

Well, I'm 63 now. Been working these 10 mu since I took over from my father in my twenties — 40 years, near enough. My wife and I handle most of it ourselves, the kids are in Handan working and don't come back much except at Spring Festival. So labor is me and her, and whatever I can hire for a few days when cotton picking comes.

My land is split like always: about 6 mu I keep in the wheat-maize rotation, and the other 4 mu stays in cotton. The western plot where I do cotton, the soil is a bit saltier and it suits cotton better than grain — I tried wheat there once in the 90s and it wasn't worth it. I don't change things without a good reason.

**Wheat** — already went in last October, around the 8th or 9th. Used mostly seed I kept back from last year's harvest plus a few kg of Jimai 22 I bought fresh to mix in, that's what most folks around here still plant. Before sowing I broadcast about 45 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind from the co-op. Now that it's spring and the wheat is greening up, I'll topdress about 18 kg of urea per mu at jointing — maybe end of March, beginning of April — and run the well on it right after. I water three times total: once before winter (already done), once with the topdress, and once at grain filling if May is dry. Extension folks used to say 18 kg of nitrogen total per mu is enough, I'm a bit above that but I'd rather spend 20 yuan extra on fertilizer than lose 50 kg of grain. I expect around 450 kg/mu if the weather cooperates — last year I got 470, year before 420.

**Maize** — goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. Window is tight, maybe 4-5 days. I don't plow, just direct-seed with the rotary planter I hire from Old Wang in the village, he charges 30 yuan/mu. I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the agro-dealer is pushing that year, they're all decent. Put 40 kg of compound at planting, then topdress 15 kg urea at the big trumpet stage in late July. Maize doesn't drink as much as wheat — one irrigation at trumpet stage if July is dry, that's usually enough here. Spray for armyworm once, weeds get a herbicide shot after planting. Looking for about 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton** — plant in mid-late April, around the 20th. Regular variety, not the expensive Bt stuff — costs too much for 4 mu, and I've been spraying bollworm myself for years, I know what I'm doing. Cotton's different from grain: you don't want to pile on nitrogen or it just grows leaves and no bolls. I do about 13 kg N/mu total, split between base and a topdress at flowering. Plow and shape beds before planting. Spray maybe 4-5 times through the season — herbicide early, then insecticide for bollworm and aphids. Pick by hand starting September, that's when I hire two neighbors for about 5 days each. Expect around 240 kg lint per mu, that's normal for my ground.

Cash-wise, whole year's input cost runs me around 4,700 yuan. Tight but manageable. If cotton prices hold up we do alright, if they drop we tighten our belt.
